# Design

Three waves. Wave 1 is the sponsored path and changes no consensus rule, so it can ship while the chain is halted and keeps working afterwards: the sponsored batch at contracts/src/BatchCallAndSponsor.sol becomes a Sidiora paymaster with a relayer-signed quote; a new Rust crate under interop/crates, modelled on the bridge relayer that already lives there, signs those quotes and submits the 7702 transactions; the TypeScript SDK gains the authorisation and quote calls; the human web application gains the journey that uses them; and the explorer learns to render a six-decimal Sidiora fee. Wave 2 is the protocol change and is written, qualified and left ready rather than deployed: the denom and its single minter, the bank-backed implementation behind the existing proxy and its pointer binding, the proxy admin behind a governance timelock, the fee-token parameters, the per-account preference precompile, the EVM fee path, the Cosmos fee path, the destination of Sidiora fees, and finally the upgrade handler that turns all of it on, the integration proof through testutil/processblock and the documentation page. Its touched paths are disjoint where the dependency graph allows, so implementation runs in parallel and only the upgrade handler and the integration proof wait for the rest. Wave 3 runs the Go, Rust and Foundry suites once on the merged revision and writes down what ran.
